Test 5
READING PASSAGE 2
You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.
COLLECTING AS A HOBBY
Collecting must be one of the most varied of human activities, and it’s one that many of us psychologists find fascinating. Many forms of collecting have been dignified with a technical name: an archtophilist collects teddy bears, a philatelist collects postage stamps, and a deltiologist collects postcards. Amassing hundreds or even thousands of postcards, chocolate wrappers or whatever, takes time, energy and money that could surely be put to much more productive use. And yet there are millions of collectors around the world. Why do they do it?
There are the people who collect because they want to make money – this could be called an instrumental reason for collecting; that is, collecting as a means to an end. They’ll look for, say, antiques that they can buy cheaply and expect to be able to sell at a profit. But there may well be a psychological element, too – buying cheap and selling dear can give the collector a sense of triumph. And as selling online is so easy, more and more people are joining in.
Many collectors collect to develop their social life, attending meetings of a group of collectors and exchanging information on items. This is a variant on joining a bridge club or a gym, and similarly brings them into contact with like-minded people.
Another motive for collecting is the desire to find something special, or a particular example of the collected item, such as a rare early recording by a particular singer. Some may spend their whole lives in a hunt for this. Psychologically, this can give a purpose to a life that otherwise feels aimless. There is a danger, though, that if the individual is ever lucky enough to find what they’re looking for, rather than celebrating their success, they may feel empty, now that the goal that drove them on has gone.
If you think about collecting postage stamps, another potential reason for it – or, perhaps, a result of collecting – is its educational value. Stamp collecting opens a window to other countries, and to the plants, animals, or famous people shown on their stamps. Similarly, in the 19th century, many collectors amassed fossils, animals and plants from around the globe, and their collections provided a vast amount of information about the natural world. Without those collections, our understanding would be greatly inferior to what it is.
In the past – and nowadays, too, though to a lesser extent – a popular form of collecting, particularly among boys and men, was trainspotting. This might involve trying to see every locomotive of a particular type, using published data that identifies each one, and ticking off each engine as it is seen. Trainspotters exchange information, these days often by mobile phone, so they can work out where to go to, to see a particular engine. As a by-product, many practitioners of the hobby become very knowledgeable about railway

Reading
operations, or the technical specifications of different engine types.
Similarly, people who collect dolls may go beyond simply enlarging their collection, and develop an interest in the way that dolls are made, or the materials that are used. These have changed over the centuries from the wood that was standard in 16th century Europe, through the wax and porcelain of later centuries, to the plastics of today’s dolls. Or collectors might be inspired to study how dolls reflect notions of what children like, or ought to like.
Not all collectors are interested in learning from their hobby, though, so what we might call a psychological reason for collecting is the need for a sense of control, perhaps as a way of dealing with insecurity. Stamp collectors, for instance, arrange their stamps in albums, usually very neatly, organising their collection according to certain commonplace principles – perhaps by country in alphabetical order, or grouping stamps by what they depict – people, birds, maps, and so on.
One reason, conscious or not, for what someone chooses to collect is to show the collector’s individualism. Someone who decides to collect something as unexpected as dog collars, for instance, may be conveying their belief that they must be interesting themselves. And believe it or not, there is at least one dog collar museum in existence, and it grew out of a personal collection.
Of course, all hobbies give pleasure, but the common factor in collecting is usually passion: pleasure is putting it far too mildly. More than most other hobbies, collecting can be totally engrossing, and can give a strong sense of personal fulfilment. To non-collectors it may appear an eccentric, if harmless, way of spending time, but potentially, collecting has a lot going for it.
21

Questions
Complete the sentences below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.

questionSections.title: Questions
questionSections.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.

questionSections.title: Questions 22–26
questionSections.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt: The writer mentions collecting ______ as an example of collecting in order to make money.
questions.evidence: They’ll look for, say, antiques that they can buy cheaply and expect to be able to sell at a profit.
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 作者提到收藏什么，作为以赚钱为目的的收藏例子？
questions.distractorAnalysis: The paragraph explicitly gives antiques as the example of buying cheaply and reselling for profit. postcards/stamps/dolls are mentioned elsewhere, but not as the money-making example.

questions.prompt: Collectors may get a feeling of ______ from buying and selling items.
questions.evidence: buying cheap and selling dear can give the collector a sense of triumph
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 收藏者通过买卖物品可能获得一种什么感觉？
questions.distractorAnalysis: feeling of paraphrases sense of; the required noun is triumph. profit is the financial outcome, not the feeling.

questions.prompt: Collectors’ clubs provide opportunities to share ______.
questions.evidence: attending meetings of a group of collectors and exchanging information on items
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 收藏者俱乐部提供分享什么的机会？
questions.distractorAnalysis: share paraphrases exchanging; information completes the sentence grammatically and semantically. items are what the information concerns, not what members share in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Collectors’ clubs offer ______ with people who have similar interests.
questions.evidence: brings them into contact with like-minded people
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 收藏者俱乐部让人们与兴趣相似者获得什么？
questions.distractorAnalysis: people who have similar interests paraphrases like-minded people; contact is the closest direct completion. The official key also accepts meetings. information belongs to Question 16 and does not fit offer ... with people.

questions.prompt: Collecting sometimes involves a life-long ______ for a special item.
questions.evidence: Another motive for collecting is the desire to find something special ... Some may spend their whole lives in a hunt for this.
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 收藏有时会涉及对某件特殊物品持续一生的什么？
questions.distractorAnalysis: life-long paraphrases spend their whole lives; hunt directly follows that wording. The official key also accepts desire. motive and recording occur in the passage but do not match the life-long search relation as directly.

questions.prompt: Searching for something particular may prevent people from feeling their life is completely ______.
questions.evidence: this can give a purpose to a life that otherwise feels aimless ... they may feel empty, now that the goal that drove them on has gone
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 寻找某件特定之物可能避免人们觉得生活完全怎样？
questions.distractorAnalysis: Having the hunt supplies purpose and prevents aimlessness; the official key also accepts empty. special/particular describe the sought item, not the person’s life.

questions.prompt: Stamp collecting may be ______ because it provides facts about different countries.
questions.evidence: another potential reason for it ... is its educational value. Stamp collecting opens a window to other countries
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 集邮可能具有什么性质，因为它能提供不同国家的相关知识？
questions.distractorAnalysis: provides facts paraphrases educational value; the adjective educational fits after may be. valuable would be a grammatical possibility but is not the passage word used for this benefit.

questions.prompt: ______ tends to be mostly a male hobby.
questions.evidence: a popular form of collecting, particularly among boys and men, was trainspotting
questions.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 14–21 on your answer sheet.
questions.translation: 什么爱好往往主要由男性参与？
questions.distractorAnalysis: particularly among boys and men paraphrases mostly a male hobby. stamp collecting and doll collecting are not assigned a predominantly male group.

questions.prompt: The number of people buying dolls has grown over the centuries.
questions.evidence: The doll paragraph discusses materials and what dolls reflect, but gives no trend in the number of buyers.
questions.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questions.translation: 购买玩偶的人数几个世纪以来一直增长。
questions.distractorAnalysis: No comparison of buyer numbers across centuries is stated. changed over the centuries refers to materials, not the number of people buying dolls.

questions.prompt: Sixteenth century European dolls were normally made of wax and porcelain.
questions.evidence: the wood that was standard in 16th century Europe, through the wax and porcelain of later centuries
questions.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questions.translation: 16世纪的欧洲玩偶通常由蜡和瓷制成。
questions.distractorAnalysis: The passage assigns wood to the sixteenth century and wax/porcelain to later centuries, directly contradicting the statement. NOT GIVEN is wrong because both the period and materials are explicitly compared.

questions.prompt: Arranging a stamp collection by the size of the stamps is less common than other methods.
questions.evidence: Examples given are country in alphabetical order and what stamps depict; size is not discussed.
questions.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questions.translation: 按邮票大小整理藏品不如其他方法常见。
questions.distractorAnalysis: The passage neither describes a size-based method nor compares its frequency. commonplace principles does not establish that sorting by size is less common.

questions.prompt: Someone who collects unusual objects may want others to think he or she is also unusual.
questions.evidence: Someone who decides to collect something as unexpected as dog collars ... may be conveying their belief that they must be interesting themselves.
questions.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questions.translation: 收藏不同寻常物品的人，可能希望别人也认为他或她不同寻常。
questions.distractorAnalysis: unusual objects paraphrases something unexpected; interesting themselves matches the desired impression about the collector. The dog-collar museum is supporting detail, not a contradiction.

questions.prompt: Collecting gives a feeling that other hobbies are unlikely to inspire.
questions.evidence: More than most other hobbies, collecting ... can give a strong sense of personal fulfilment.
questions.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage on pages 20 and 21? In boxes 22–26 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questions.translation: 收藏能带来一种其他爱好不太可能激发的感受。
questions.distractorAnalysis: More than most other hobbies means this strong fulfilment is comparatively unlikely to come from other hobbies. All hobbies give pleasure, but the passage distinguishes the intensity of collecting.
